Raw Material Techpacks – Materials. Every material the T-shirt needs is created once as its own techpack: one fabric and three trims. The BOM lines point to these article codes.
Apparel Techpack – Detail. The garment itself. It fixes buyer, colour card, size range and purchase UOM – everything below inherits these.

BOM · Materials – Materials (4). One line per material: how much one T-shirt consumes, with wastage, and what it costs. Value flows to the Cost tab; each line is linked to a process on the Routing tab.

BOM · Materials – Consumption chain – worked example (Cons 2). One line per material: how much one T-shirt consumes, with wastage, and what it costs. Value flows to the Cost tab; each line is linked to a process on the Routing tab.
BOM · Routing · Processes – Processes (3). The processes that make the T-shirt, in order. Each Process Rate comes from its operation (Cost Of × Production Time) and is summed into Production Cost.
BOM · Routing · Operations – Operations (3). Operation parameters per process: machine, efficiency, Cost Of and time. Cost Of × Production Time becomes the Process Rate.
BOM · Routing · Material Linkage – Materials (4). Each BOM line is mapped to the process that consumes it – the fabric is issued to cutting, thread and cufflinks to sewing, the polybag to packing.
BOM · Cost – Materials by section. Material value by section plus process rates give the Total Cost per piece, which is compared with the selling price after and before discount.
BOM · Cost – Production cost (3). Material value by section plus process rates give the Total Cost per piece, which is compared with the selling price after and before discount.
BOM · Cost – Cost summary. Material value by section plus process rates give the Total Cost per piece, which is compared with the selling price after and before discount.
BOM used by the order – Materials (1). The Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58) BOM line that the booking, MRP and FPO quantities are exploded with: 1.5 KG_Nis of N-8 per shirt.
Buyer Block Booking – Material Details (6). Fabric booked per colour/size before the order exists. Indented Qty is written back from the Adhoc Indent.
BBB Adhoc Indent – Indent lines (6). Raised from the booking ("Generate Indent Requirement"). Each line points back to a booking material line; Ordered Qty comes back from the PO.
RMPO 1229 – Article Detail (6). Purchase order for the booked fabric. Value uses the PO price (10), not the indent rate (5). Shipped Qty comes back from the GRN.
GRN – GRN Qty (6). Fabric received against RMPO 1229. Accepted qty becomes stock under the stock key, still tagged with booking PPJ179.
Sales Order (OC) – Add Quantity BreakUp (4). The confirmed buyer order: pieces per colour × size. Confirming it runs MRP.

MRP – Level 1 – Garment (4). Level 1 = garments to make (from the OC). Level 2 = fabric to buy: garment qty × BOM final consumption. Running Level 1 for the full qty generates the child indents. Any level can take a negative, but a child indent is reduced or cancelled only by a negative at its parent level, and only after MRP is re-run.

MRP – Level 2 – Fabric N-8 (4). Level 1 = garments to make (from the OC). Level 2 = fabric to buy: garment qty × BOM final consumption. Running Level 1 for the full qty generates the child indents. Any level can take a negative, but a child indent is reduced or cancelled only by a negative at its parent level, and only after MRP is re-run.

MRP – Adjustment scenarios (Level 1 = 500). Level 1 = garments to make (from the OC). Level 2 = fabric to buy: garment qty × BOM final consumption. Running Level 1 for the full qty generates the child indents. Any level can take a negative, but a child indent is reduced or cancelled only by a negative at its parent level, and only after MRP is re-run.
Sales Order Indent – Indent lines (4). MRP Level 2 written as an indent. Booking stock with the same stock key is reserved first (In-house Adj.); only the rest is ordered.
RMPO 1230 – Article Detail (4). Purchase order only for the part of the sales-order indent not covered by booking stock.
FPO – FPO Qty – Colour/Size (4). Pieces released to the factory, the fabric they need, and how much of it is already reserved versus still on order.
FPO – Stock Material Allocation (4). Pieces released to the factory, the fabric they need, and how much of it is already reserved versus still on order.
